findings.claim: The two domains share one rule vocabulary, so a law minted in one can be judged by the other.
findings.headline: Jaccard 0.17 over 121 ops — the banks are largely disjoint vocabularies

findings.claim: A kernel law can be re-derived in the tensor bank.
findings.headline: 28/49 kernel ops (57%) have no tensor spelling — those laws cannot cross without translation

findings.claim: The derivability union the novelty sieve computes is a real floor, not a formality.
findings.headline: 3/3 shipped kernel laws are derivable from the 374-rule union — the floor demotes them to known

findings.claim: Crossing works through explicit denotation rows: a kernel law is provable in the union even though the tensor bank cannot spell its fused op.
findings.headline: every derivable law has a prior-art witness (`pa_kf_*_expand`) — translation rows, not a shared vocabulary, are what make the union real
